statement: Create and edit materials from up to six asset types: identity, graphics (surface and cut patterns), appearance, physical, thermal and (2027) carbon.
superiority: Keep one open material definition shared across tools with explicit asset provenance.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Original omits the carbon asset. Acceptance sketch: A new material shows its surface pattern in a shaded view and its asset values in the schedule.

statement: Set line weight, colour, pattern and material per category and subcategory for model, annotation and imported objects.
superiority: Preview style changes live across sheets before applying.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Changing Walls cut line weight changes every wall cut in all views.

statement: Configure object snaps (endpoints, midpoints, centres, intersections, nearest) and snap increments.
superiority: Show a snap ranking overlay and reduce ambiguous snaps.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Snap to midpoint lands within 1e-6 of the segment midpoint.

statement: Maintain project name, number, address, client and issue date parameters used in title blocks and tags.
superiority: Sync project information with an external project record.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Project name appears in the title block on every sheet.

statement: Set display units and formats per discipline for length, area, volume, angle, slope and others.
superiority: Offer discipline unit presets that switch in one click.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Setting millimetres displays model length in mm with the chosen decimals.

statement: Define line weights, line patterns and line styles used across the project.
superiority: Share a standards file across projects.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Weight table entry changes printed width at the view scale.

statement: Define drafting and model fill patterns for surfaces and regions.
superiority: Import hatches from standard pattern files.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Pattern spacing equals definition at scale.

statement: Define arrowhead styles (arrow, dot, tick, slash) with size and fill used by dimensions and leaders.
superiority: Support custom arrowhead shapes shared through office standards.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Arrowhead drawn size in mm equals the setting at plot scale.

statement: Maintain revisions in a Sheet Issues/Revisions dialog on the View tab, setting numbering scheme, date, description, issued-to and issued-by, and whether the cloud and tag display.
superiority: Immutable issued records.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Located on View > Sheet Composition, not under Manage > Additional Settings. Acceptance sketch: Issue date shows on the revision table.

statement: Choose whether temporary dimensions measure to wall centre, core face or other references.
superiority: Remember per element type and show the active reference in the tooltip.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Temporary dimension to a wall reads the distance to the chosen reference.

statement: Open structural settings for symbolic representation, load cases and boundary conditions.
superiority: Single modern settings pane.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Setting opens and values persist.

statement: Relocate the project in shared coordinates by specifying a point and rotating true north.

source.ref: Relocate the Model by Specifying Coordinates

superiority: Georeference with EPSG code and transformation shown.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Acquired point equals shared coordinate within 1e-3.

statement: Choose the view that opens when the project is opened.

source.ref: Specify the Starting View for a Model

superiority: Allow a per-user start view saved in preferences.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Project opens in the configured view.

statement: Select an element by its Element ID and show it in the active view.
superiority: Search by GUID, Mark or any parameter value in one box.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: The element with the entered ID is selected and the view zooms to it.

statement: Every element has a project-local element ID plus a separate stable unique ID string that survives upgrades and central saves, usable for external references.
superiority: Expose stable IDs through open APIs.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: UniqueId is documented as stable across upgrades and workset operations while ElementId may change; 'GUID-like' is not stated. Acceptance sketch: UniqueId persists across save and copy.

statement: Group, sort and filter the project browser's views, sheets and schedules using organization schemes built from their properties and project parameters.
superiority: Save organisations as views.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Applies to views, sheets and schedules/quantities, not families. Acceptance sketch: Browser tree reflects the rule.

statement: Save a selection as a named set and reload it later.
superiority: Dynamic selection sets defined by rules.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Loaded set equals saved elements.

statement: Filter a multiple selection by category to keep only certain types.
superiority: Query by parameter value too.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Filter keeps only chosen categories.

statement: Manage and run C# macros held in application-level modules through the Macro Manager, which opens an external code editor for authoring and debugging.
superiority: Run scripts in a permissioned sandbox with the same API as add-ins.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: 2027 documents only application-level modules; project-level scope not found. Acceptance sketch: A macro bound to a button modifies a parameter on the selected element.

statement: Enable or disable application-level macros (disabled by default), with changes taking effect after Revit restarts.
superiority: Sandbox scripts with explicit permission prompts rather than all-or-nothing levels.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Documented as a simple enable/disable switch; signing levels and add-ins are not mentioned. Acceptance sketch: Unsigned macro is blocked at the highest level.

statement: Provide an add-ins manager that lists loaded add-ins and macros with load times and lets the user enable or disable them individually or all at once, effective next launch, also as a standalone tool.
superiority: Package manager with signed add-ins and version pinning.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Page is about enabling/disabling add-ins, not about running external tools. Acceptance sketch: Add-in appears on the ribbon.

statement: Set notification, save reminder, username, journal and synchronisation defaults.
superiority: Sync settings across machines with the user account.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Save reminder fires at the configured interval.

statement: Configure tab visibility, keyboard shortcuts and recent file lists.
superiority: Share shortcut maps and import other tools' shortcut sets.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: A custom shortcut triggers the assigned command.

statement: Set view-navigation performance options, anti-aliasing, and temporary dimension text size and background on the Graphics tab, with accelerated graphics enablement also managed from that tab.
superiority: Auto-configure by detecting the GPU and warn about unsupported drivers.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Background colour is not documented on this tab (the background option is for temporary dimension text). Acceptance sketch: Changing the setting takes effect after restart and persists.

statement: Accelerated graphics became a fully supported mode in 2027 for modeling and navigation, adding section box, halftone, transparency and linked-model improvements, with an optional Vulkan engine setting.

source.ref: Accelerated Graphics Graduates from Tech Preview

superiority: GPU renderer that keeps 60 frames per second on 100 million triangles.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: It graduated from tech preview in 2027 (introduced in 2026) rather than being new in 2027. Acceptance sketch: Viewport on a large model reaches the frame-time budget.

statement: The Options Bar is removed in 2027 and its controls move to the Properties palette and the ribbon.

source.ref: Streamlined User Interface: Options Bar Removal

superiority: Place contextual options near the cursor with a fixed escape hatch.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Original said contextual properties and in-canvas controls; page says Properties palette and ribbon. Acceptance sketch: Each former option bar setting is reachable in the new location.

statement: Add-ins run on .NET 10 in 2027 requiring recompiled plug-ins.
superiority: Stable ABI across versions to avoid the annual add-in migration.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: A sample plug-in recompiled for the new runtime loads.

statement: Choose the section head family used by section tags and the callout head family and bubble corner radius used by callout tags through the Section Tags and Callout Tags settings.
superiority: Provide a gallery of tag styles with live sample.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Naming of views is not part of these settings; callout side documented on About Callout Tags. Acceptance sketch: A new section uses the selected head family.

statement: Set project location by address or latitude and longitude to drive sun path and weather data.

source.ref: Location and Site Dialog: Location Tab

superiority: Pick the location on a map with a time-zone and elevation lookup.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Sun position at noon equals the astronomical value for the entered latitude.

statement: Rotate project north relative to true north and keep views oriented to either.

source.ref: About Project North and True North

superiority: Display a visual compass and warn about mismatched orientation among links.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: A 30-degree true north rotates the sun path by 30 degrees.

statement: Search the Project Browser for views, sheets and families by text.
superiority: Use fuzzy and parameter-aware search with saved queries.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Search returns exactly the items whose name contains the text.

statement: Export warnings attached to selected elements to a report file for reference.
superiority: Offer machine-readable export with stable element identifiers and run-to-run diffs.
notes: ADDED 2026-11-14: feature found documented in Revit 2027 help during the verification pass; not in the original register Acceptance sketch: Export warnings for a selection and confirm each warning lists its elements.

statement: Report the numeric ID of the selected elements in a dialog for troubleshooting.
superiority: Also copy IDs and unique IDs to the clipboard with one click.
notes: ADDED 2026-11-14: feature found documented in Revit 2027 help during the verification pass; not in the original register Acceptance sketch: Select a wall, run the tool and see its ID; paste it into Select by ID to find it again.

statement: A cloud-connected add-in reports health, performance and usage of cloud models for a single model, a project or an organisation without opening Revit, flagging problems such as sudden file growth.
superiority: Run the same checks locally and offline.
notes: ADDED 2026-11-14: Revit 2027 What’s New feature with no matching row in the original register Acceptance sketch: Open a model whose size doubled and see the analytics report name the cause.

statement: Viewer mode is removed from Revit 2027, with browser-based viewing and shared views suggested as replacements.
superiority: Offer a free offline read-only mode with no licence needed.
notes: ADDED 2026-11-14: Revit 2027 What’s New feature with no matching row in the original register Acceptance sketch: Confirm a viewer-only launch path exists without a paid seat.
